close_reason: Replaced the match-on-Option in parse_issuing_dp with the canonical Option::map().transpose() recipe. Functionally identical; expression form is one chain.
description:
## Location
pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:708-729 — fn parse_issuing_dp.

## Finding
```
let ext = crl.tbs_cert_list.crl_extensions.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[])
    .iter().find(|e| e.extn_id == OID_ISSUING_DISTRIBUTION_POINT);

match ext {
    None => Ok(None),
    Some(e) => {
        let idp = IssuingDistributionPoint::from_der(e.extn_value.as_bytes())
            .map_err(|e| Error::CrlParseError(crate::DerError(e)))?;
        Ok(Some(idp))
    }
}
```

This is the canonical 'Option<T> + (T -> Result<U, E>) -> Result<Option<U>, E>' shape. Idiomatic Rust uses Option::map followed by Option::transpose:

```
crl.tbs_cert_list.crl_extensions.as_deref().unwrap_or(&[])
    .iter()
    .find(|e| e.extn_id == OID_ISSUING_DISTRIBUTION_POINT)
    .map(|e| IssuingDistributionPoint::from_der(e.extn_value.as_bytes())
        .map_err(|err| Error::CrlParseError(crate::DerError(err))))
    .transpose()
```

Functionally identical. The map+transpose form:
- Is one expression, no intermediate let binding.
- Removes the explicit None match arm.
- Is the standard recipe in std-lib doc examples for this exact transformation.

## Counter-argument
The match form is arguably more obvious to readers unfamiliar with .transpose(). The current code is correct and readable.

## Severity
P4 (pure stylistic / opinion). No correctness, perf, or API impact. clippy does not flag it (option_map + transpose is not a configured lint).

## Recommendation
Defer or close as opinion. File for completeness as part of the rusty pass.
title: (IDIOM) P4: parse_issuing_dp match-on-Option could be Option::map().transpose()
